first_step_test: A small central head, tapered body, and two connected upper wing arcs fix the moth's size and symmetry without guessing detached parts.

source.notes: Four generated raster attempts (three sheets and one targeted edit) repeatedly shifted wing/head anchors between rows or introduced later-stage details early. No approved contact sheet or public art; image-generation continuity blocker on 2026-10-05.

final_elements.name: head and tapered body
final_elements.description: Round head above a narrow vertical abdomen, fixed at page center.

final_elements.name: left upper wing
final_elements.description: Broad upper wing arcs from the left shoulder and returns to the body.

final_elements.name: right upper wing
final_elements.description: Mirrors the left upper wing at the same height.

final_elements.name: left lower wing
final_elements.description: Rounded lobe attached below the left upper wing.

final_elements.name: right lower wing
final_elements.description: Rounded lobe attached below the right upper wing.

final_elements.name: left antenna
final_elements.description: Short feathery antenna rising from the left side of the head.

final_elements.name: right antenna
final_elements.description: Short feathery antenna rising from the right side of the head.

final_elements.name: window crossbars
final_elements.description: One vertical and one horizontal faint window bar, interrupted behind the moth.

final_elements.name: four wing eyespots
final_elements.description: One small paired spot in each of the four wings.

final_elements.name: wing veins
final_elements.description: A few short graphite veins radiating from the body into each wing.

frames.step_name: Place the moth's center and upper wings
frames.visible_job: Draw the fixed head, tapered body, and two broad upper wing outlines.
frames.instruction: Draw a small round head and tapered body at the center. From each shoulder, sweep a wide upper wing outward and back toward the abdomen at matching heights.

frames.visible_job: Add two smaller rounded lower wing lobes below the upper wings.
frames.instruction: From each lower shoulder, curve a smaller rounded lobe outward, then bring it back to the lower body. Keep both upper wings unchanged.

frames.visible_job: Grow a short feathery antenna from each side of the head.
frames.instruction: Draw two short antenna stems upward from the head. Add a few tiny feather strokes along each stem, leaving the four wing contours in place.

frames.visible_job: Place a faint vertical and horizontal window bar behind the moth.
frames.instruction: Draw a light vertical bar above and below the moth, stopping at its wing edges. Add a horizontal bar to either side, also stopping where the wings overlap it.

frames.visible_job: Add four separate small eyespots and a few veins inside the existing wings.
frames.instruction: Put one small oval eyespot in each of the four wings. Draw a few short veins from the body toward the edges, stopping before the outlines.

final_step.visible_job: Deepen the existing keeper lines and shade within the four wing shapes.
final_step.instruction: Deepen the head, body and four wing edges, then add restrained graphite and warm gray pencil shading inside the established wings. Leave the eyespots and window bars readable; add no new structure.
